after.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}z+2y+7x=1 \\ 3y-z=-2 \\ 4y-2z-3x=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}7x+2y+z=1 \\ 3y-z=-2 \\ -3x+4y-2z=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ -3 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ -3 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =7|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =7(-6+4)-2(-3)+1(9) \\  & =-14+6+9 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 9 \\ -8 & -11 & 34 \\ -5 & -7 & 21\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 9 \\ 8 & -11 & -34 \\ -5 & 7 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 25 \\ 77\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-18,\,y=25,\,z=77.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
content.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}z+2y+7x=1 \\ 3y-z=-2 \\ 4y-2z-3x=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}7x+2y+z=1 \\ 3y-z=-2 \\ -3x+4y-2z=0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ -3 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \\ -3 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =7|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}|+1|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =7(-6+4)-2(-3)+1(9) \\  & =-14+6+9 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ -3 & -2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}7 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & -3 & 9 \\ -8 & -11 & 34 \\ -5 & -7 & 21\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 & 9 \\ 8 & -11 & -34 \\ -5 & 7 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 8 & -5 \\ 3 & -11 & 7 \\ 9 & -34 & 21\text{ }\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18 \\ 25 \\ 77\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=-18,\,y=25,\,z=77.$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3z-y+x-5=0 \\ y+2x+2z=1 \\ z-2x-2y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=5 \\ 2x+y+2z=1 \\ -2x-2y+z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(1+4)+1(2+4)+3(-4+2) \\  & =5+6-6 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 & -2 \\ 5 & 7 & -4 \\ -5 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -6 & -2 \\ -5 & 7 & 4 \\ -5 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -\frac{19}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=3,y=-\frac{19}{5},z=-\frac{3}{5}.$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a 3x3 System of Equations By Calculating the Inverse of the Coefficient Matrix
content.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}3z-y+x-5=0 \\ y+2x+2z=1 \\ z-2x-2y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
content.worked_solution:
We organize the system so that it’s in the correct order first:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=5 \\ 2x+y+2z=1 \\ -2x-2y+z=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-(-1)|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|+3|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(1+4)+1(2+4)+3(-4+2) \\  & =5+6-6 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 6 & -2 \\ 5 & 7 & -4 \\ -5 & -4 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}5 & -6 & -2 \\ -5 & 7 & 4 \\ -5 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -5 \\ -6 & 7 & 4 \\ -2 & 4 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -\frac{19}{5} \\ -\frac{3}{5}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=3,y=-\frac{19}{5},z=-\frac{3}{5}.$

after.problem:
Solve the following system of linear equations by finding the inverse of the coefficient matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-z=0 \\ x+y+3z=2 \\ 3x-2y+z=4\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
after.worked_solution:
We wish to write this system in the form $Ax=b$, where $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and $x$ and $b$ are $3\times 1$ column vectors. We can do this as follows:

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, the solution to $Ax=b$ is given by $x={A}^{-1}b.$ So, we compute ${A}^{-1}$ as follows:

*Step 1:*

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-0|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(1-3(-2))+0-1(-2-3) \\  & =1+6+2+3 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 2:*

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\ |\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}| & |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}7 & -8 & -5 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

*Step 3:*

$$
C=[\begin{aligned}7 & 8 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \\ 1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 4:*

$$
{C}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & 4 & -4 \\ -5 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Step 5:*

$$
{A}^{-1}=\frac{1}{det(A)}{C}^{T}=\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & 4 & -4 \\ -5 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}7 & 2 & 1 \\ 8 & 4 & -4 \\ -5 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -8 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Hence the solution is $x=\frac{2}{3},y=-\frac{2}{3},z=\frac{2}{3}.$

after.problem: Consider a matrix equation ${A}^{-1}B\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $6\times 6$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $6\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
after.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${A}^{-1}B\,x=d$ by $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}B\,x & =d \\ A{A}^{-1}B\,x & =A\,d \\ {I}_{6}B\,x & =A\,d \\ B\,x & =A\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x=A\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & =A\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ {I}_{6}\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Solving a Matrix Equation Using Algebraic Manipulation
content.problem: Consider a matrix equation ${A}^{-1}B\,x=d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $6\times 6$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $6\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
content.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${A}^{-1}B\,x=d$ by $A,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1}B\,x & =d \\ A{A}^{-1}B\,x & =A\,d \\ {I}_{6}B\,x & =A\,d \\ B\,x & =A\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $B$ is not singular, it must have an inverse ${B}^{-1}.$ Now, pre-multiplying both sides of the equation $B\,x=A\,d$ by ${B}^{-1},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}B\,x & =A\,d \\ {B}^{-1}B\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ {I}_{6}\,x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d \\ x & ={B}^{-1}A\,d.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: Consider a matrix equation ${B}^{-1}\,x=A\,d,$ where $A$ and $B$ are $9\times 9$ non-singular matrices, while $x$ and $d$ are $9\times 1$ column vectors. Solve the equation for $x.$
content.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying both sides of the equation ${B}^{-1}\,x=A\,d$ by $B,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{-1}\,x & =A\,d \\ B{B}^{-1}\,x & =BA\,d \\ {I}_{9}\,x & =BA\,d \\ x & =BA\,d.\end{aligned}
$$
